scope: Full Apollo game audit and repairs on TEST only

fixed.finding: Merch could start outside before admission, while the state reducer refused to bank those points.
fixed.change: All game entry paths now share admission checks and an actionable next step.

fixed.finding: A non-object scoreboard save could throw before the game opened.
fixed.change: Validate stored rows, preserve valid names and scores, and recover from malformed data.

fixed.finding: Result and share content overflowed the fixed arena; inactive Eli pads continued taking space.
fixed.change: Scroll result content, hide inactive result controls, and increase download-link contrast.

fixed.finding: Eli and merch started immediately while other artist games waited for Start.
fixed.change: All ten rounds wait for an explicit Start tap.

fixed.finding: A failed audio download incorrectly prompted the player to enable music.
fixed.change: Connection and autoplay failures now give different retry guidance.

fixed.finding: Muted previews had no visible local sound toggle, and playback could continue when the tab was hidden.
fixed.change: Add master-sound control, accurate muted status, hidden-tab pause, and cleanup.

fixed.finding: Initial image loading provided no visible progress and an unresolved decode could stall startup.
fixed.change: Show progress, bound loading, keep entry controls disabled until ready, and provide reload recovery; decode reused scenery once.

fixed.finding: A failed device save referred to an unconnected online scoreboard.
fixed.change: Explain that the night was not saved, keep the current tab open, and offer a device-save retry.

coverage: all nine artist games plus merch
silent video loop and playback suspension

remaining: First-time loading is still heavy on slow connections: about 11.55 MB of images before character selection. Staged room/asset loading is the next performance priority.
Phone checks used Chrome touch emulation, not physical iPhone Safari or Android devices.
No 100K concurrent-player or launch-bandwidth test was performed. The scoreboard remains device-only.
Game-rule tests and automated playthroughs do not establish human difficulty balance or replay enjoyment; a short fresh-player playtest remains useful.
Canvas games have keyboard controls, but this was not a complete assistive-technology accessibility certification.
